contents.text:
# LogSeq MCP guide

Read-only access to a LogSeq graph. Nothing here edits it.

Start with:
- "what do I know about X": logseq_explore_context (one page; call it once per page, in parallel, for several)
- keywords: logseq_find_blocks
- journals and "last week": logseq_query_by_date_range
- unsure of a page name: logseq_find_pages
- "this page": logseq_get_current
- a long page: logseq_get_page with detail "outline", then logseq_get_block on the uuids you pick

Reading results:
- Page names are case-insensitive. Block uuid is the stable id; numeric id is internal.
- ((uuid)) in content is a block ref. Fetch it with logseq_get_block, or pass resolve_refs (get_page, get_block, explore_context, query_by_date_range) to get resolvedRefs.
- A warning means the result was cut or partial. hasMore: true means a parameter can fetch more (howToFetchAll says which); with hasMore: false the warning says why not (narrow the request). Check warnings before saying something doesn't exist.
- Search is literal (no synonyms) and traversal only follows [[links]] and #tags.
- A trailing meta block may carry tips for a next call. Ignore them if unhelpful.

## Tools

- logseq_find_pages: Find non-journal pages as { name, aliases? }. Filters AND: text (substring of name or alias); names (up to 50, exact name or alias; each answered with its page, or null plus closest names); property + value (page property).
- logseq_get_current: Get what the user is looking at in LogSeq right now: the open page, the block being edited, and any selected blocks.
- logseq_get_graph: Get the connected graph's name and filesystem path.
- logseq_get_page: Get a page by name (case-insensitive). detail: page (default), full (adds its blocks) or outline (top-level blocks: uuid, first line, child count).
- logseq_get_block: Get one block by UUID, optionally with its children. UUIDs come from other results and from ((uuid)) refs in content.
- logseq_find_blocks: Find blocks, newest first. Filters AND (one or more): text (substring, case-insensitive); page; links_to (1-5 pages; [[x]] or #x, not plain text); property + value (exact); period on journals (start_date + end_date, last_n days or preset). Pages by limit (max 500) and offset: check hasMore.
- logseq_query_by_date_range: Query journal entries by start_date + end_date, last_n journals, or a preset (give exactly one), with optional search.
- logseq_explore_context: Explore one page: its blocks, related pages and references (blocks linking to it, most-linking pages first; page with references_offset).
- logseq_get_concept_network: Map pages linked to a concept as nodes and edges, in both link directions, up to max_depth hops. One edge per page pair, with a reference count.
- logseq_search_by_relationship: Find whether topic A connects to topic B within max_distance link hops (connected-within, the only type). If so, returns the blocks of both pages. Both topics must be pages. Capped by limit (max 500): see warnings.
- logseq_get_concept_evolution: Track a concept over time: blocks on its page and blocks linking to it, grouped by day, week or month, with optional date bounds.
- logseq_check_links: Check a [[link]] pass. ok is true only if after strips back to before, brackets balance and don't nest, every ref in before is kept, and each [[term]] names exactly one page or alias.

## Prompts

- weekly_summary: Summarize a Monday-to-Friday week of journal entries into a few short signals. Defaults to this week.
- monthly_summary: Summarize a month from its weekly summary pages, stating the trajectory of each thread. Defaults to this month.
- continue_on: Pick up where I left off on a topic: current state, latest activity, open tasks and a suggested next step.
- what_do_i_know: Research a topic across the graph: notes, connections and gaps, with sources.
- prioritize_tasks: Find open TODO and DOING tasks, spot stale ones and suggest what to do next.

## Resources

- logseq://guide: this guide
- logseq://page/{name}: one page as text (URL-encode the name; aliases and ISO dates work)
